import type { ReviewSettingsSnapshot } from "./settings.js";
import type { MemoryStore } from "../../store.js";
import type { PluginLog } from "../../services/plugin-log.js";
import type { HostContext } from "../../index.js";
/**
 * Mount the card routes on the host web server through a nested inject, so
 * the plugin stays mountable on hosts without that service. Called once the
 * store is ready — the memory routes are projections of the store, not of files.
 *
 * The card's opening workspace comes from the host registry, read through
 * `ctx.get` on every request (the FAQ #2 sibling-service rule — the service is
 * optional, so it must not join the inject list, which would gate the mount).
 * The review-settings route is global (no `root`): reads come from the entry's
 * live volatile reader, writes merge through `configEditor.edit` so the profile
 * patch stays the single source of truth. A host without `configEditor`
 * keeps the memory card; the settings POST then answers 503.
 */
export declare function mountCardWhenAvailable(host: HostContext, store: MemoryStore, readReviewSettings: () => ReviewSettingsSnapshot, log: PluginLog): void;
/**
 * Take the plugin's settings page policy: the settings card inside the
 * bundle page is the only settings UI, so the host must not auto-generate a
 * second form page for the volatile fields (the default-model precedent:
 * `settings.configure({ auto: false }, ownFiber)`). A host without the
 * `settings` service keeps its default behavior — injection and tools are
 * unaffected.
 */
export declare function mountSettingsPresentation(host: HostContext, log: PluginLog): void;

/**
 * The clock every prompt is anchored to: the run's baseline day and the line
 * that hands it to the model.
 *
 * The model has no clock of its own. A direct LLM call carries an instruction
 * and a user prompt and nothing else — no runtime context, no timestamps — so
 * "is this date in the future?" is answered from the model's own prior unless
 * the caller says otherwise. A run resolves its day once at the boundary and
 * carries it as data, so a replay and a live run see the same prompts.
 */
/**
 * The current UTC day `YYYY-MM-DD`.
 *
 * UTC is the plugin's unit: the review account's day uses the same value, so
 * one run cannot straddle two dates.
 *
 * @returns Today's date in UTC.
 */
export declare function todayUtc(): string;
/**
 * The date-baseline line appended to the instruction of a job that makes
 * time-relative judgments.
 *
 * It names the day *and* says which side of it is a defect, because the rule
 * being protected is "no future dates", not "never touch dates": the 2026-10-14
 * trial produced 8 of 13 rewrite verdicts that stripped correct past dates as
 * if they were future ones.
 *
 * @param today - The run's baseline day `YYYY-MM-DD` (UTC).
 * @returns The instruction line to append to a system prompt.
 */
export declare function dateBaseline(today: string): string;
modules.src/services/retention.ts:
/**
 * How long the plugin keeps its own ledgers, and when it prunes them.
 *
 * `MemoryStore.pruneLedger` shipped with no production caller, so "the ledgers
 * are pruned" was true of the API and false of the machine (2026-10-14 real
 * store: 547 extraction rows in 9 days, 115 review rows in 3). Retention is a
 * policy with a trigger, and the trigger is the part that was missing.
 *
 * The check is day-throttled and idempotent, so every writer can call it
 * cheaply and a long-running process prunes without a scheduler of its own.
 */
import { type MemoryStore } from "../store.js";
/** Rows older than this many days are pruned. */
export declare const LEDGER_RETENTION_DAYS = 30;
/** How long a spent route-failure record is kept before the sweep drops it. */
export declare const FAILURE_STATE_RETENTION_DAYS = 7;
/**
 * Prune the ledgers, the plugin log, and the spent route-failure records when
 * this UTC day has not been pruned.
 *
 * @param store - The store to prune.
 * @param now - The instant to judge by (defaults to the wall clock; tests pass one).
 * @returns Rows removed, or 0 when today's prune already ran.
 */
export declare function pruneIfDue(store: MemoryStore, now?: Date): number;
/**
 * Drop the route-failure records whose backoff ended long ago: those sessions
 * never came back, and one `state` row per dead session is the kind of growth
 * that outlives its usefulness.
 *
 * @param store - The store to sweep.
 * @param nowMs - Epoch ms to judge by.
 * @returns Records dropped.
 */
export declare function pruneFailureState(store: MemoryStore, nowMs: number): number;

/**
 * The tiering exits of the review ring (`2026-10-13-memory-tiering-and-promotion`,
 * `2026-10-17-review-and-tiering-batch-rollout` §R2): archive, promote, demote,
 * and the probation resolution a `keep` verdict triggers.
 *
 * Every exit writes one verdict row in the partition the move happened in, and
 * that row is also the "already judged" marker: a promoted row is not brand
 * new (it keeps its history), an archived row leaves every queue, and a demoted
 * row does not look like a drop-in on its way back. Nothing here deletes: the
 * archive is a status bit and the source row keeps its body.
 */
import type { ReviewItem } from "./review-ring.js";
import type { EvolveVerdict } from "./review-prompt.js";
/**
 * Land the exits that move a memory between layers or out of the queue.
 * @param item - The review item whose verdict asked for a move.
 * @param verdict - The verdict this item produced.
 * @returns True when the verdict was one of the tiering exits and is handled.
 */
export declare function landTieringExit(item: ReviewItem, evolved: EvolveVerdict, verdict: "archive" | "promote" | "demote" | "keep" | "export-suggestion"): boolean;
